text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Mining leader WMC Ltd has reduced its dividend after falling gold and nickel prices slashed the group's profits by 23 per cent in 1996-97. WMC's net profit for the 12 months to June 30 fell from A$386.2 million to A$297.2 million despite the steady profits from its alumina and aluminium assets. Page 21.

Trans-Tasman brewer Lion Nathan refused to comment yesterday on rumours of a take-over bid by a European brewer. The speculation coincides with the persistent industry belief that Lion Nathan's biggest shareholder and chief executive Doug Myers wishes to reduce his holding in the company. Page 21.

BHP has appointed BHP Engineering, led by group general manager Geoffrey Knox, to take control of the A$1.65 billion hot briquetted iron project in Western Australia. The project has suffered massive cost blowouts of up to A$300 million. Page 22.

Rural Press Ltd attempted to quash market speculation it was preparing to sell its radio assets. In a statement released in response to an inquiry by the Australian Stock Exchange into the 21 per cent rise in its share price over the last six weks, Rural Press said its recent US$57 million acquisition of the Farm Progress Group of Companies could explain the development. Page 22.

The A$350 million five-year financing package offered by Rupert Murdoch to merge the Super League competition with the Australian Rugby League (ARL), may disappoint the earning expectations of the ARL's 14 clubs. The package will be negotiated today betwen executives from the two leagues. Page 22.

Cable manufacturer Metal Manufactures Ltd has reduced its dividend after posting a 20 per cent fall in interim net profit to A$15.7 million for the first six months to June. Managing director Glenn Dudley predicted an improved company performance in the second half of the year. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Commonwealth Bank of Australia is planning to buy back A$650 million of its shares and use other excess capital to invest in an external technology supplier. CBA revealed the plan yesterday after announcing a four per cent drop in net profit fo the year to June 30. Page 19.

Institute of Public Affairs executive director Mike Nahan said yesterday business investment could increase by hundreds of millions of dollars through Federal Government tax reforms. Referring to the Federal Government's tax reform proposals Nahan stressed a review should consider all taxes which affected investment decisions, particularly those pertaining to State systems. Page 19.

Infrastructure Trust of Australia, a division of Macquarie Bank's Macquarie Infrastructure Investment Management, has posted a A$27.9 million net profit by including a A$10 million abnormal writedown derived from its listing last December. The result means a 5.5 cent a unit dividend will be issued compared with the 5.33 cent dividend forecast in the prospectus. Page 21.

Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer has warned the grain industry that it must develop a united position on the restructuring of the Australian Wheat Board. The warning was issued yesterday following an announcement by the West Australian Farmers Federation it was withdrawing from national talks. Page 21.

Cigarette manufacturers have claimed higher Federal Government excise charges, brought in to replace the outlawed State Government licence fees, will result in them paying an extra A$500 million in tax. Page 22.

Croesus Mining plans to increase gold production and reduce costs at its Binduli gold mine in Western Australia through a A$4.1 million upgrade of its Hannan South treatment plant. The upgrade will allow an increase in the processing of oxide ore into prmary ore of 500,000 tonnes annually. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Commonwealth Bank has announced a four per cent drop in annual earnings, the first for a major bank since 1992, and has warned shareholders of further difficult trading conditions. The fall in earnings derives from falling lending profit margins and igher expenses. Page 29.

Goodman Fielder chairman David Clarke told an Australian Institute of Company Directors lunch yesterday directors should be paid on the basis of their company's performance. One of the three companies with which he is involved plans to introduce the system within the next 12 months. Page 31.

Australia's third largest telecommunications company AAPT announced yesterday it would invest A$305 million in the growth of the industry. The investment would be made into the information and telecommunications industry over the next five years. Page 31.

Cable maker Metal Manufactures has reported a 20.3 per cent fall in half-year profits to A$15.7 million, forcing it to cut its dividend from six cents to five cents a share. The poor result has been blamed on the sluggish Australian economy and turmoil in major Thai markets. Page 31.

Qantas Airways has finalised negotiations with major shareholder British Airways that will see code-share agreements introduced on flights between Brisbane, Singapore and London. Code-sharing allows two companies to buy seats on each other's flights. Pag 31.

Australian confectionery trading levels for 1995 and 1996 have been outstanding with retailers achieving record sales and product volume. Market leader Cadbury is confident sales will continue to rise as outlined in their 1997 yearbook. Page 32.
THE AGE

The Commonwealth Bank of Australia yesterday announced a A$1078 million net profit which included a A$128 million write-off of obsolete technology. The result is due to strong lending growth and a rigorous control of costs. Page C1.

Gold mining company Croesus Mining NL yesterday announced a A$4.1 million upgrade of its Hannan South treatment plant in Western Australia. The move will allow an expansion of gold production at its Binduli gold mine to the processing of 500,000 tonnes of gold ore a year. Page C3.

Goodman Fielder chairman David Clarke yesterday called for company directors pay levels to be linked to their organisation's performance. Clarke, who also chairs Brian McGuigan Wines and is executive chairman of the Macquarie Bank, also called for similar assessment of individual board members. Page C3.

The Australian Shareholders Association has called for companies to disclose details of political donations in their annual reports. Association executive officer Tony McLean says disclosure is necessary as shareholders should be kept informed on how ther funds were spent. Page C3.

Global mining giant WMC Ltd yesterday announced an equity profit for the year to June of A$228.2 million. The disappointing result was due to the fall in prices across all of the group's products and a high U.S. exchange rate. Page C3.

The White Foil gold discovery by Melbourne-based Mineral Commodities NL and French mining giant Cogema has been confirmed as a major deposit. The partners yesterday announced a initial resource estimate for White Foil of 873,881 ounces of gold. Page C3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
